key_insight: MINDSET treats long-term conversational memory as a constrained state-evolution problem, storing immutable episodes and updating versioned schemas only when the minimum-energy transition is justified.
engineering_relevance: This enables memory systems for agents to preserve both current and historical knowledge, reduce unnecessary LLM rewrites, and retrieve stale-versus-active information more reliably.
method: Stores each conversation turn as an immutable episode
Organizes episodes into versioned schemas with transitions that can reinforce, supersede, split, or create schemas
Selects updates by balancing distortion, contradiction, historical damage, fragmentation, and inconsistency with hysteresis
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 850 questions across LoCoMo and MemoryAgentBench, MINDSET achieved the best observed LoCoMo answer F1 and improved retrieval metrics (Recall@8, MRR, nDCG@8) over LightMem, with cross-model validation on 700 questions using GLM-4.7 and Gemma-4-31B.
watch_item: The approach adds decision logic for schema transitions, so practical deployment must manage computational overhead and avoid brittle behavior when memory evidence is sparse or highly contradictory.
paper_title: MINDSET: Energy-based Schema Evolution for Long Conversational Agent Memory
